title: Effective quasiparticle conserving Lindbladians in the thermodynamic limit
abstract: Open quantum many-body systems are commonly described by Lindblad master equations, yet the treatment of Lindbladian operators in the thermodynamic limit remains a major challenge. We develop a framework for constructing effective quasiparticle-conserving Lindbladian operators directly in the thermodynamic limit. Our approach extends continuous similarity transformations to non-Hermitian open quantum systems and enables the systematic block diagonalization of Lindbladians with respect to the quasiparticle (qp) number. We formulate two complementary methods. The first, projective continuous similarity transformations (pcst++), generalizes perturbative continuous unitary transformations to Lindblad operators so that a linked-cluster expansion allows us to obtain high-order series expansions of the infinite system. The second, deepCST, extends directly evaluated enhanced perturbative continuous unitary transformations by combining the same qp-conserving generator with a perturbative truncation scheme that yields non-perturbative effective Lindbladian operators directly in thermodynamic limit. We apply pcst++ and deepCST to the dissipative transverse-field Ising chain with local dissipation. We focus on the low-Ising regime. We purify the Lindbladian by splitting each spin into two sites. A spin flip then corresponds to two qps. We derive and analyze the effective, qp-conserving Lindbladian in the sectors with zero to two qps. We show how the Ising interaction renormalizes the decay rates of elementary spin-flip excitations and provides the microscopic mechanism for a competition between coherent interactions and dissipation. Our work establishes perturbative and non-perturbative continuous similarity transformations as a versatile tool for deriving effective qp pictures of open quantum many-body systems in the thermodynamic limit.
summary: This paper introduces advanced theoretical techniques, pcst++ and deepCST, to calculate effective quasiparticle-conserving Lindbladians for open quantum many-body systems in the thermodynamic limit. By applying these methods to the dissipative transverse-field Ising model, the authors demonstrate how to systematically handle dissipation while preserving the quasiparticle structure. This establishes a versatile tool for studying non-equilibrium steady states in complex quantum materials.
main_problem: The primary challenge addressed is developing a systematic framework to construct effective quasiparticle-conserving Lindbladian operators directly in the thermodynamic limit for open quantum many-body systems.
main_result: The authors successfully developed and applied two complementary methods, pcst++ and deepCST, demonstrating they can derive effective Lindbladians that preserve quasiparticle number in the thermodynamic limit.
method: The core methodology involves extending continuous similarity transformations (CSTs) from Hermitian Hamiltonians to non-Hermitian Lindbladians, enabling block diagonalization with respect to the quasiparticle number.
model_or_system: The study uses the dissipative transverse-field Ising chain (DTFIM) with local dissipation as a paradigmatic model. The system is analyzed by purifying the Lindbladian and mapping it to a quasiparticle basis.
key_observables: The primary observables are the eigenvalues ($\lambda$) of the Lindbladian, from which the decay rates (inverse lifetimes) of elementary excitations are extracted. The Liouvillian gap is also a key diagnostic.
important_parameters: The analysis focuses on the thermodynamic limit and treats the Ising interaction ($J$) as a small perturbation in the low-Ising regime.
main_assumptions: The methods assume that the continuous similarity transformations can be systematically applied to the non-Hermitian Lindbladian structure, and the analysis relies on perturbative expansions (linked-cluster/flow equations).
figures_summary: Figure 8 compares the calculated inverse lifetime of the longest-living state in the 2-qp sector as a function of the coupling $J$ using both pcst++ (solid lines) and deepCST (scatter plots) expansions, showing convergence up to $J \approx 0.4$.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem, details the two complementary theoretical frameworks (pcst++ and deepCST), applies these methods to the DTFIM, and analyzes the resulting effective Lindbladian structure and its spectral properties.
why_interesting: This work provides powerful, generalizable theoretical tools (pcst++/deepCST) for analyzing non-equilibrium steady states in interacting quantum systems, which is crucial for understanding open quantum dynamics in condensed matter.

The colored solid lines represent k = 0 and the colored dotted lines k = π. The respective thin black lines represent the highest diagonal Padé approximants of the highest order pcst++ series. The scatter plots represent the deepCST expansion up to different orders. The bigger black markers represent k = 0 and the smaller gray markers k = π. Orders lower than 4 are not plotted.
